items.title: William "Big Bill" Thompson Interview, 1961-03-01
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] ...he played like baby Bruce and Boyle and different.

ctx.x: Well, I'll tell you, I'll tell you, I had the biggest surprise of my time playing, the big surprise I had was one day I was, I passed one day up on Orleans Street. And at that time, I'd see the fellow because he was called Walter. And Walter used to be playing on the piano all the time. And I said, I got there and I said, well, he saw me, he said, Mr. Bill, he said, stop, he said, stop a minute, he said, yeah, I'm playing. He said, listen, let me play. He said, I'll play. And when I went inside, I fought with…
He was hard to have. He played way different from what he's playing now. See, in that case, he played like baby Bruce and Boyle and different.

I told Walter, I said, he'd be great. But he did grow up to be good too. He said, I hear him 9, 11, 9, and I hear him over the television, on the radio, I hear him playing. He said, yeah, he's good. Walter's wonderful.
